title: gaussian_splatting: render splats with the engine's TAA jitter, and key the render cache on the matrix that carries it (#929)
abstract:
Splats swim under FSR2 because the projection uploaded to the splat GPU pipeline never carried the engine's temporal jitter. This lands the fix, the cache-key change that would otherwise have silently neutered it, a QA oracle that is red on the unfixed tree, and the scoped disclosure of the half that remains.

**Base:** `b915afc51c5` (origin/master at the time of writing; top commits #999 and #1009).
**Why one PR and not a stack.** The plan this follows is four ordered steps — rig, cache key, jitter, disclosure — and the rig is deliberately **red on the unfixed tree**. A blocking QA scene that fails on master cannot land on its own, so splitting the rig out would either red master or require landing it disabled, which is the opposite of the point. The four steps are still separable in review: §4.1 is the rig, §3 change 2 is the cache key, §3 change 1 is the jitter, §5 is the disclosure, and §4.3 shows each production change failing its own test in isolation.

**Risk class:** R2 — `python scripts/agentic/classify_change.py` returns **R2** for this path set (`renderer/**`). Note that `interfaces/output_compositor.{h,cpp}`, which this PR also touches, classifies **R1** under the misclassification filed as **#1017**; it is treated as R2 here regardless and carries the GPU evidence below.

---

# 1. The defect, re-verified at the base

`gaussian_splat_renderer.cpp:2400-2402` built the GPU projection by copying `p_render_data->scene_data->cam_projection` (`:2373`) and flipping one sign:

```cpp
// Apply flip_y only; gaussian pipeline uses linear view-space depth.
Projection render_projection = cam_projection;
if (... scene_data->flip_y) { render_projection.columns[1][1] = -render_projection.columns[1][1]; }
```

`grep -c taa_jitter modules/gaussian_splatting/` returned **0** — not one reference in the module.

Meanwhile every mesh in the same frame is rendered through `RenderSceneDataRD::get_cam_projection()` (`servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/render_scene_data_rd.cpp:40-45`), which left-multiplies `taa_jitter` via `Projection::add_jitter_offset()` (`core/math/projection.cpp:932-935`), and FSR2 is handed the same vector immediately below the splat pre-upscale hook (`render_forward_clustered.cpp:2699`, `params.jitter` at `:2713`). FSR2 then **un-jitters** its input — `ComputeHrPosFromLrPos()` at `thirdparty/amd-fsr2/shaders/ffx_fsr2_common.h:431-437` and `InitParams()` at `ffx_fsr2_accumulate.h:219-220`. A layer that was never jittered is therefore reconstructed displaced by `+jitter`, moving every frame along the Halton sequence.

Godot's TAA never receives the jitter at all — the whole push constant at `servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/effects/taa_resolve.glsl:50-55` is `{vec2 resolution; float disocclusion_threshold; float disocclusion_scale;}` — so under TAA splats do not swim; they are bit-stable and simply never antialiased. **The issue title is half wrong and the §11 entry is updated to say so.**

---

# 2. Measurement

## 2.1 Real scan, before and after

**Binaries** (both built by me from this repo in the same worktree, `platform=windows target=editor optimize=speed_trace tests=yes module_gaussian_splatting_enabled=yes gs_native_arch=no` — **not** a dev build, so not `-O0`):
- BASE: `b915afc51c5`, `Z:/wt-929-bin/base/godot.windows.editor.x86_64.exe`, 178,642,432 bytes, linked 2026-09-17 23:09:26.
- AFTER: `f10ac3c6ecf`, `Z:/wt-929-bin/fixed/godot.windows.editor.x86_64.exe`, 178,658,304 bytes, linked 2026-09-17 23:17:01.

**Which commit produced which measurement**, because the head moved twice after the real-scan capture (once to recalibrate the QA gate, once for the self-review fixes in §8) and an evidence chain that does not say so is not one:

| measurement | commit it was taken at | production-code delta to this PR's head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| §2.1 real-scan capture, BASE | `b915afc51c5` | the whole PR |
| §2.1 real-scan capture, AFTER | `f10ac3c6ecf` | **none** — `git diff f10ac3c6ecf HEAD -- modules/gaussian_splatting/renderer modules/gaussian_splatting/interfaces` is comments only |
| §4.1 QA rig, BASE and AFTER; §4.2 lane counts; §4.4 full suite | `a7e21559f63` | **none** — comment-only |
| §4.3 mutations | `5dcb353dc4b` + one reverted line each | the §8 review fixes, none of which touch the mutated lines |

The base binary independently reproduces the assessment's published numbers, which were measured on the **nightly** (`5dfeb44b5b4`, a different binary built on different hardware): 0.000 / 0.002 / 1.089 / 1.409 mean LSB with peaks 104 and 136, to the digit. Two independently built binaries agreeing to three decimal places is the cross-check that the rig is measuring the renderer and not the build.

**GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, Vulkan driver 1.4.325. **Renderer:** `forward_plus`.
**Scene:** one real-scan `GaussianSplatNode3D` (`Cabin in the forest.ply`, **31,208 visible splats** in both runs, `quality/preset = 2`) **plus** a high-frequency checker-textured unshaded box, both in one 960×540 `SubViewport` (`own_world_3d`, `transparent_bg = false`), **static camera** (near 0.05, far 200), static content.
**Project pins in force:** this rig's `project.godot` pins **nothing** under `[gaussian_splatting]`, so `composite/depth_test` runs at its shipped default `true` (`core/gaussian_splat_manager.cpp:998`) and `per_splat_depth_clip` at its shipped default `true` (`:1002`). It is deliberately **not** the QA project, which pins `composite/depth_test=false`, `lighting/indirect_sh_scale=0.0` and `use_rgba8_framebuffer=true` — the masked configuration that hid GPU-001 twice.
**Method:** 24 consecutive frames per config after a 64-frame warm-up, plus an 8-frame engage window captured right after each switch; metrics computed offline over a splat-only mask (264,185 px) and a mesh-only mask (45,802 px) derived from reference captures. The mesh is the in-frame control: same frame, same stage, same capture path, drawn with the engine's jitter-corrected projection.
Run under the shared heavy lock with CI idle.

**BASE — `b915afc51c5`, binary `godot.windows.editor.x86_64.exe` 178,642,432 bytes, linked 2026-09-17 23:09**

| config | scale | raster path | SPLAT Δ LSB mean / max | MESH Δ LSB mean / max | **SPLAT displacement px mean / max** | MESH displacement px mean / max | autocorr @ jitter phase, splat / mesh |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| none | 1.00 | other | **0.000** / 0 | 0.000 / 0 | **0.0000** / 0.0000 | 0.0000 / 0.0000 | n/a |
| taa | 1.00 | other | **0.002** / 14 | 0.310 / 59 | **0.0000** / 0.0000 | 0.0151 / 0.0314 | +0.985 / +0.981 |
| fsr2 | 1.00 | other | **1.089** / 104 | 2.365 / 123 | **0.2525** / 0.3945 | 0.0100 / 0.0198 | **+1.000 / +1.000** |
| fsr2 | 0.50 | other | **1.409** / 136 | 2.180 / 220 | **0.3603** / 0.7015 | 0.0046 / 0.0119 | n/a (phase 32 > window) |

**AFTER — `f10ac3c6ecf` (C++ identical to the head of this PR; the later amend touched only the two QA `.gd` files, `git diff --stat` confirms), binary 178,658,304 bytes, linked 2026-09-17 23:17**

| config | scale | raster path | SPLAT Δ LSB mean / max | MESH Δ LSB mean / max | **SPLAT displacement px mean / max** | MESH displacement px mean / max | autocorr @ jitter phase, splat / mesh |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| none | 1.00 | other | **0.000** / 0 | 0.000 / 0 | **0.0000** / 0.0000 | 0.0000 / 0.0000 | n/a |
| taa | 1.00 | other | **0.098** / 14 | 0.407 / 59 | **0.0156** / 0.0360 | 0.0152 / 0.0315 | +1.000 / +0.992 |
| fsr2 | 1.00 | other | **0.894** / 103 | 2.306 / 121 | **0.0900** / 0.1469 | 0.0099 / 0.0172 | +1.000 / +0.999 |
| fsr2 | 0.50 | other | **0.977** / 133 | 1.909 / 220 | **0.0927** / 0.1790 | 0.0046 / 0.0075 | n/a |

(Δ = per-channel LSB, 0–255, mean over consecutive-frame pairs in the mask. Displacement = Lucas–Kanade sub-pixel shift of each captured frame against that window's own mean frame, in output pixels.)

**What moved, and what did not:**

| | BASE | AFTER | |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| FSR2 @1.0 splat displacement | 0.2525 px | **0.0900 px** | −64%, a 2.8× reduction; peak 0.3945 → 0.1469 px |
| FSR2 @0.5 splat displacement | 0.3603 px | **0.0927 px** | −74%, a 3.9× reduction; peak 0.7015 → 0.1790 px |
| FSR2 @1.0 **mesh control** | 0.0100 px | 0.0099 px | unchanged — the change is confined to the splat layer |
| FSR2 @0.5 **mesh control** | 0.0046 px | 0.0046 px | unchanged |
| **no temporal stage** | 0.0000 px / 0.000 LSB | 0.0000 px / 0.000 LSB | bit-identical, both regions, as the zero-jitter short-circuit guarantees |
| **TAA** splat | 0.0000 px / 0.002 LSB | 0.0156 px / 0.098 LSB | **not a regression — the intended effect.** Splats were bit-stable under TAA because they were never jittered, i.e. never antialiased while every mesh beside them was. They now move by the same order as the mesh control (0.0156 vs 0.0152 px in this run), which is what a correctly integrated layer looks like. Read as an order of magnitude, not a parity claim: the TAA control has run-to-run spread comparable to its own value (an independent reproduction measured 0.0068 / 0.0182 px), and TAA is not gated. |
| **TAA** mesh control | 0.0151 px | 0.0152 px | unchanged |

**The residual is named, not hidden.** After the fix the splat layer still displaces ~0.09 px against a mesh control at ~0.01 px. That remainder is not the jitter. **#1025 later identified the mechanism**, and it is not the one guessed here: the composite already feeds FSR2's reactive mask through the destination alpha (`viewport_blit.glsl:206-208` → `params.reactive`), clamped to 0.9, so FSR2 is *deliberately not accumulating history* on splat pixels — they track the raw jittered frame instead of converging the way the mesh does. An earlier revision of this paragraph blamed "no reactive mask", which was false. That is the §8.1 disclosure and the follow-up issue, not a defect this PR leaves half-fixed.


## 2.2 Why the colour delta is reported and not gated

Look at the BASE FSR2 rows: the **broken** splat region measures 1.089 mean LSB while the **correct** mesh control beside it measures 2.365. The broken layer scores better. Mean |LSB| between consecutive frames confounds displacement with local contrast, and a 2 px checker has a far larger gradient than a soft scan. Gating it in either direction would be gating content.

## 2.3 Why the periodicity is reported and not gated either

The assessment attributed the defect by periodicity: the splat signal repeats with period 8 at scale 1.0, autocorrelation **+1.00** at lag 8, which is the engine's jitter phase (`renderer_viewport.cpp:252-260`). That attribution is sound and I reproduced it.

It is not an **oracle**, and this is the one place my verification contradicts the assessment's plan, which proposed it as the QA rig's oracle ("the splat-region signal's autocorrelation at the engine's jitter-phase lag … is the oracle"). Measured on the same captures, the **mesh control** autocorrelates **+1.000** at lag 8 as well. FSR2's resolve is phase-periodic under a static camera whether or not the layer feeding it is jittered, so the statistic cannot separate a correctly integrated layer from a broken one, and a gate built on it would have been red before and after. The QA rig records both autocorrelations and gates on neither; the reasoning is written into the scene header so the next reader does not rediscover it as a good idea.

## 2.4 What does separate: sub-pixel displacement

The defect is a statement about position, so measure position. A first-order (Lucas–Kanade) estimate divides the temporal difference by the spatial gradient and returns **pixels**, so contrast cancels:

```
[Sxx Sxy; Sxy Syy] d = [bx; by],  Sxx = sum gx^2 ... bx = sum gx * dI
```

evaluated for each frame of the converged window against that window's own mean frame. Those are the `SPLAT px` / `MESH px` columns above.

---

# 3. The change

**1. `GaussianSplatRenderer::build_render_projection()`** (`renderer/gaussian_splat_renderer.cpp`, declared beside `build_cull_projection()`). Static and free of `RenderData`, so the contract is unit-testable without a GPU. It applies `flip_y` and, when the jitter is non-zero, the same identity-plus-translation correction the engine uses. It deliberately does **not** apply the engine's depth correction — the gaussian pipeline carries linear view-space depth.

Zero jitter short-circuits and returns the flipped matrix, so the non-temporal path is bit-identical to the pre-#929 matrix **by construction** rather than by a floating-point argument about multiplying by an identity. It is self-gating: `scene_data->taa_jitter` is exactly `(0,0)` unless a temporal stage is active (`renderer_scene_cull.cpp:2681-2696` only assigns it when the jitter phase count is non-zero; `renderer_viewport.cpp:252-260` leaves that at 0 unless temporal upscaling or TAA is on). The shadow pass (`gaussian_splat_renderer.cpp:1981-1987`) builds its own projections locally and is untouched.

**2. The render cache reuse key now carries the GPU projection** (`interfaces/output_compositor.{h,cpp}`, call sites at `renderer/render_pipeline_stages.cpp:1909` and `:2603`). The key was `p_input.projection`, the **unjittered** camera projection, compared exactly at `output_compositor.cpp:176`. The jitter appears nowhere else, so wherever reuse is live — a static camera, which is exactly the case this fix is about — the raster stage is skipped (`render_pipeline_stages.cpp:1835`) and one frozen jitter phase would be re-composited every frame. Change 1 would silently do nothing while still looking correct to any test that only inspects the matrix the renderer built. The new parameter is **required and has no default**, so a caller cannot reintroduce the trap by forgetting an argument.

**3. Three false comments.** `gaussian_splat_renderer.h:377`, `interfaces/rasterizer_interfaces.h:34` and `interfaces/painterly_renderer_interfaces.h:88` all read `// GPU projection with depth/jitter correction applied.` The code had never applied either.

## 3.1 Blast radius, checked rather than assumed

| consumer | projection | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU/CPU cull, frustum planes | `cull_projection`, re-derived from the unjittered projection (`gaussian_splat_renderer.cpp:588-595`) | unaffected; `tests/ci/check_cull_signature_parity.py` green |
| `_compute_cull_config_signature` | zero occurrences of "projection" in the function | unaffected |
| depth sort keys | view-space z only (`compute/depth_compute.glsl:202-203`) | unaffected |
| conic / Jacobian / subpixel-cull | `focal_x/y` from `projection_matrix[0][0]`/`[1][1]` (`shaders/tile_binning.glsl:566-568`) — the two entries the jitter provably does not touch, asserted in the new unit test | unaffected |
| near/far | `p_params.projection.get_z_near()/get_z_far()` (`tile_render_stages.cpp:278-279`), the unjittered one, and unaffected by a translation anyway | unaffected |
| shadow pass | builds both projections locally with `p_render_data == nullptr` | unaffected |
| tile binning grid | `render_projection` (`tile_binning.glsl:541`, `:557-558`) | **affected, and correctly so** — binning and raster share one matrix, which is what makes the layer move as a unit |
| painterly raster | same `TileRenderer::RenderParams` | follows automatically |
| `tile_resolve.glsl:276` lighting reconstruction | `params.inv_projection_matrix` | **checked, and the assessment's concern does not apply.** `tile_render_stages.cpp:251-262` derives both `projection_matrix` and `inv_projection_matrix` from the same `render_projection`, so the forward and inverse stay a consistent pair; inverting the jittered matrix at the pixel centre is the correct recovery for a fragment produced by the jittered forward transform. |
| composite depth test | `viewport_blit.glsl:120-135` compares GS depth against the engine's scene depth | **improves.** Godot's opaque depth buffer is jittered whenever TAA/FSR2 is on, so before this the two sat in different subpixel frames. This is also why the jitter must be taken from `scene_data` verbatim: a rescaled or negated value would misregister silhouettes instead of fixing them. |

`tests/ci/check_gs_pre_upscale_hook.py` watches seven literal anchors in `render_forward_clustered.cpp`; this PR touches none of them and the guard is green.

## 3.2 Performance

The render cache is **already disabled at shipped defaults** and was never the cost it looked like: `_is_per_splat_clip_expected()` (`render_pipeline_stages.cpp:234-249`) returns true whenever `per_splat_depth_clip` is on — shipped default `true` (`core/gaussian_splat_manager.cpp:1002`) — and `:2598-2600` then refuses reuse outright for non-painterly frames. Measured rather than inferred: every config in every capture above reported `raster_path = other`, never `cached`. The static-camera render cache never engaged once.

---

# 4. Tests, and the proof each one is not vacuous

## 4.1 The QA rig — `qa_composite_production_defaults`, phase 2

The scene keeps its presence phase unchanged and gains a temporal-stability phase: a 480×270 `SubViewport` with its own `World3D`, carrying a deterministic high-contrast splat cluster on the left and a high-frequency checker-textured **unshaded** box on the right, in **disjoint screen rectangles of one frame**, swept over `{none, taa, fsr2@1.0, fsr2@0.5}`. It sets `composite/depth_test` to the shipped default `true` for the sweep and restores the project pin afterwards, and the runner already requires config-mutating scenes to run last. Both phases now call `_finish_test()` when done, so the suite does not pay for the raised `test_duration` ceiling — **the whole scene runs in 11 s**.

Run standalone, both with **this PR's rig** — the same two `.gd` files — differing only in which binary renders them: the §2.1 BASE binary (`b915afc51c5`) and a build of `a7e21559f63`, which is this PR's head minus comments (see the provenance table in §2.1).

| | `none` | `taa` | `fsr2 @1.0` | `fsr2 @0.5` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **BASE splat px** | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | **0.3052** | **0.2219** |
| **AFTER splat px** | 0.0000 | 0.0209 | **0.0929** | **0.0614** |
| mesh control px, BASE → AFTER | 0.0000 → 0.0000 | 0.0092 → 0.0092 | 0.0029 → 0.0030 | 0.0034 → 0.0042 |
| mesh engage-window Δ LSB | 0.000 | 0.190 | 3.146 | 5.922 |
| splat / mesh autocorr @ jitter phase | n/a | unavailable¹ | **+1.000 / +1.000** | unavailable¹ |

¹ the 16-frame window yields 15 pairs and `autocorrelation_at_lag` needs 4 overlapping pairs, so the largest usable lag is 11 — below the TAA phase (16) and the FSR2 @0.5 phase (32). The scene records the *reason string* for those two rather than a number, so "could not be measured" and "measured and came out flat" cannot be confused. Lengthening the window to cover lag 32 would cost this blocking lane ~2.5× for a statistic that is not gated, and that cost is declined in the code.

**BASE verdict:** `FAIL: … TEMPORAL STABILITY failed: fsr2_100: the splat layer displaces 0.3052 px against its own window mean, over the 0.150 px ceiling, while the in-frame mesh control … displaces 0.0029 px. The splat projection is not carrying the engine's taa_jitter (#929). | fsr2_050: … 0.2219 px …`
**AFTER verdict:** `PASS: … temporal stability OK: none splat=0.0000px mesh=0.0000px, taa splat=0.0209px mesh=0.0092px, fsr2_100 splat=0.0929px mesh=0.0030px, fsr2_050 splat=0.0614px mesh=0.0042px`

The **FSR2** mesh-control values, the engage deltas and the autocorrelations repeat to the third digit across the two runs, so in the two configurations the gate actually reads, only the splat layer moved — the single-variable property the rig exists to establish. **The TAA mesh control does not repeat that tightly** and the sentence here originally over-claimed it: my two runs both read 0.0092 px, but the independent reviewer's reproduction measured 0.0068 px on base and 0.0182 px on final. TAA is reported and not gated, so nothing depends on it; the honest statement is that the TAA control has run-to-run spread of the same order as its own value, and that FSR2 — the gated pair — does not.

**Threshold calibration, every observation.** On one RTX 3090 / Vulkan 1.4.325, `optimize=speed_trace`:

```
jitter ABSENT   fsr2_100: 0.3045 0.3066 0.3047 0.3052 0.3041 0.3066 0.3047
                fsr2_050: 0.2444 0.2347 0.2252 0.2219 0.2172 0.2403
jitter APPLIED  fsr2_100: 0.0929 0.0929 0.0929 0.0929 0.09286
                fsr2_050: 0.0542 0.0569 0.0614 0.0570 0.0545
```

The last two `fsr2_100` entries per row and the last `fsr2_050` entries were taken **after** the stray GPU process was killed, and are indistinguishable from those taken under it — the measurement, not the argument, that this metric does not respond to contention. `0.09286` / `0.0545` come from a CI run on a **`dev_build`** binary rather than `optimize=speed_trace`.

0.15 px is within 6% of the geometric midpoint of the two nearest neighbours across that whole set (`sqrt(0.0929 × 0.2172) = 0.142`): **1.61× above every passing measurement and 1.45× below every failing one.** The `0.3041 / 0.2252` pair comes from a mutation build that reverts only the jitter, so the defect population is not merely "an older tree". The same numbers, and the instruction to widen rather than delete if another GPU ever reds a correct tree, are in the constant's docblock.

**Which project pins are active here**, because this is the QA project and its pins have hidden real defects twice. `tests/examples/godot/test_project/project.godot` pins `composite/depth_test=false`, `renderer_rd/forward_plus/use_rgba8_framebuffer=true`, `lighting/indirect_sh_scale=0.0`, `lighting/shadow_strength=0.0`, plus the `gpu_sorting` block. Phase 2 **overrides `composite/depth_test` to the shipped `true`** for its sweep and restores the pin in `_restore_settings()`; **every other pin stays active**, including `use_rgba8_framebuffer=true`. That last one was the live risk — an RGBA8 internal buffer could plausibly have made FSR2 refuse to run, and a silently-not-running FSR2 leaves a perfectly stable splat region that looks exactly like a perfectly integrated one. It does not: the engage gate measures the mesh control moving by 3.146 and 5.922 LSB in the two FSR2 windows, so the stage demonstrably ran under that pin. That is the gate earning its place rather than a box ticked.

**Three gates run before any displacement is scored**, and each fails the scene rather than degrading:

1. **Rig determinism** — with no temporal stage both regions must be bit-identical frame to frame (`0.000` LSB mean *and* max). Measured exactly 0 in every run.
2. **Region discrimination** — hiding the splat node must move the splat rectangle by ≥ 1.0 LSB and the mesh rectangle by ≤ 0.5, and vice versa. Without it both rectangles could be pointing at background and every number below would be noise compared with noise.
3. **Stage engaged** — the mesh control must move during each temporal config's engage window. A viewport that silently refuses TAA or FSR2 leaves both layers perfectly stable, which is indistinguishable from perfect integration; this is #997's shape and it is directly reachable here.

A region whose gradient energy or structure tensor cannot support the 2×2 solve is reported `UNMEASURABLE` **and fails**; it is never recorded as `0.0 px`, which would read as flawless stability.

## 4.2 Unit tests — both in the STRICT `[ViewTransform]` lane, both without a GPU

`[GaussianSplatting][ViewTransform] Render projection carries the engine TAA jitter` (`tests/test_view_transform.h`), four subcases — zero jitter is **bit-identical** to the flip-only matrix in all 16 entries (and to the raw matrix with `flip_y = false`); a non-zero jitter composes exactly as `J · (flip · P)`; the result is a **depth-independent** NDC translation of exactly `+jitter` at three depths spanning 0.5 to 100 m, with `w` unchanged and `columns[0][0]` / `columns[1][1]` untouched; and two different phases produce different matrices. It carries its own discrimination check — that the jittered and unjittered matrices differ at all — so a no-op implementation cannot satisfy the equalities.

The fourth subcase uses an **off-axis frustum** (`set_frustum(2.0, 16/9, Vector2(0, 0.3), …)`, which writes a non-zero `columns[2][1]`) and `REQUIRE`s that entry is really non-zero before asserting, per column, that the jitter contribution is exactly `+jitter × w_row` and that zero jitter is still bit-identical. It exists because the symmetric perspective is precisely the case where the module's single-entry flip and the engine's whole-row flip agree, so on its own it could not pin down what the jitter does for any other projection type. The **jitter term** is the engine's for all of them; the **flip** is not, and that divergence is pre-existing, unchanged here, and now named in the docblock rather than papered over (self-review finding 1).

`[GaussianSplatting][ViewTransform] Render cache reuse is refused when only the GPU projection's jitter differs` (`tests/test_renderer_pipeline.h`) — drives `OutputCompositor` **before `initialize()`**, so with `p_require_valid_depth = false` the two cache functions are pure functions over the cache state and need no `RenderingDevice`; RIDs come from a local `RID_Owner`. It asserts reuse is *granted* for an identical key in both directions before asserting it is *refused* when only the jitter moves, so it cannot be satisfied by a cache that never grants reuse. It is tagged `[ViewTransform]` deliberately: `[Renderer]` is an advisory lane (`run_module_tests.py`, `strict=False`) and a fail-closed proof that cannot fail CI is not a proof.

Lane counts on the same filter (`--test-case=*GaussianSplatting*][ViewTransform]* --test-case-exclude=*][RequiresGPU]*`): **5 cases / 5 assertions at base → 7 cases / 78 assertions after, 7 passed, 0 failed.** The two new cases contribute 73 assertions, so they are not empty shells.

## 4.3 Mutation proofs

Each mutation reverses **exactly one** production change and leaves the tests in place, so the failure attributes to that change rather than to "something broke". The edits are exact-string patches that refuse to apply unless the anchor is found exactly once — a mutation that silently did nothing cannot be mistaken for "the test still passed". Each is a full `optimize=speed_trace` rebuild, ~35 s incremental, and the binary's link time was checked before each run.

**Mutation 1 — drop the GPU-projection compare from the reuse key** (removes the five added lines in `OutputCompositor::can_reuse_cached_render`; the jitter itself is still applied).


**Reading implemented: the rule keeps its force and gains one narrow, explicitly-stated exception** — rather than moving #1025 into §11. The exception requires **all four** of: the defect is a *residual* of something already fixed (shipped behaviour strictly better, not merely documented); closing it needs a *higher risk class than the fix itself* (R3 at the engine boundary, ADR required); a *workaround exists and is stated*, reachable from default settings; and **a named human has accepted it as an alpha limitation**, recorded on the issue or the PR.

I did not make the product call, and this PR does not contain a human decision dressed up as one. The §10.1 envelope bullet now says on its face that it is **an agent's transcription of a decision relayed from the maintainer**, and that the maintainer's own line on #929 or #1026 is the authoritative record — the review's objection was that a release-scope decision had no human trace, and the fix for that is to label the transcription as one, not to make it look more official. **What happens to #929 on merge** — the review asked, and §11 item 5 now answers it explicitly. The review was right that §3.2 argued cost ≈ 0 from the shipped-default path and never took the number the plan's step 2 asked for. Taken now — and then **retaken**, because the first measurement was contaminated (see the note at the top of the table).

> **These figures were re-measured on 2026-09-20 and the delta moved.** A stray `godot.head.exe` from 2026-09-16 had been holding the GPU on this machine for three days; it was killed on 2026-09-20. The **pixel and displacement** measurements everywhere else in this PR are deterministic frame comparisons and are unaffected — as is the `cached` / `other` structural result below, which is a count, not a time. The superseded figures were +2.11 ms (0.798 → 2.912) against +1.87 ms (0.905 → 2.772) now; the conclusion did not change and its margin got tighter.

**Configuration:** the same real scan (31,208 splats, 960×540 `SubViewport`, static camera), `optimize=speed_trace`, RTX 3090, **vsync off** (without that every number is the monitor), 240 timed frames per config after a 40-frame settle, `raster_path` sampled every 8th frame across the window rather than once. **Six samples per binary per config**, taken under the shared heavy lock with CI idle and no other GPU process on the box.

**With the relief valve OFF (`composite/per_splat_depth_clip = false`) — the only shipped way to make static-camera reuse live:**

| config | BASE ms/frame | BASE raster | AFTER ms/frame | AFTER raster |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| no temporal stage | 0.680–0.955 (mean 0.804) | `cached` **30/30** | 0.692–0.954 (mean 0.851) | `cached` **30/30** |
| FSR2 @1.0 | 0.759–1.176 (mean **0.905**) | `cached` **30/30** | 2.735–2.881 (mean **2.772**) | `cached` **0/30** |

**At SHIPPED DEFAULTS (`per_splat_depth_clip = true`) — the control:**

| config | BASE ms/frame | BASE raster | AFTER ms/frame | AFTER raster |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| no temporal stage | 2.612 / 2.613 | `cached` **0/30** | 2.605 / 2.624 | `cached` **0/30** |
| FSR2 @1.0 | 2.737 / 2.780 (mean 2.758) | `cached` **0/30** | 2.745 / 2.774 (mean 2.760) | `cached` **0/30** |

**At shipped defaults the two binaries are indistinguishable** — 2.758 vs 2.760 ms under FSR2, 2.613 vs 2.615 with no temporal stage. The cache never engages on either, exactly as §3.2 claimed; that claim is now measured on both sides rather than argued from one code path.

Three things follow, and the first is the one that matters:

1. **The base binary's "cheap" FSR2 row is the defect, not a baseline.** `cached 30/30` under FSR2 means the raster never re-ran while the Halton phase advanced — one frozen jitter phase re-composited every frame, for as long as the camera stays still. That is precisely what the cache-key change exists to stop. The comparison is not "0.9 ms versus 2.8 ms", it is "0.9 ms for a wrong image versus 2.8 ms for a right one".
2. **The cost is real and bounded: +1.87 ms/frame** (0.905 → 2.772 mean) in that configuration, on this scene. Worst pairing across the samples is +2.12 ms, best is +1.56 ms. The spread is almost entirely on the *cached* side, which is a sub-millisecond path dominated by CPU and present jitter (0.759–1.176, 55%); the re-raster side is steady (2.735–2.881, 5%).
3. **It is not a new cost, it is the shipped-default cost reappearing.** The relief-valve-off AFTER figure (2.772 ms) and the shipped-default figure (2.758 / 2.760 ms) agree to within 0.5%: turning the valve off no longer buys a static-camera saving under a temporal stage, so that configuration now performs as the shipped default already does. Nothing got slower than the product's own baseline; one opt-out stopped paying off, and it was only paying off by serving a stale frame.

**With no temporal stage the key change is inert** — `cached 30/30` on both binaries, and the spread within each binary is larger than the gap between them. That is what the zero-jitter short-circuit guarantees, now measured rather than argued.

`docs/architecture/render-pipeline.md` now states the behaviour and these numbers; neither it nor the setting's docstring said that static-camera reuse is unavailable under a temporal stage.
